q-36947.name: Question 1
q-36947.problem:
$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 2 \\ 9 & -6 & -9 \\ 1 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

The vector $v$ and the matrix $A$ are given above. 
If $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =3,$ then what is the value of $\frac{b}{c}?$
q-36947.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =3.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 2 \\ 9 & -6 & -9 \\ 1 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}]-3[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 9 & -9 & -9 \\ 1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{3}=0 \\ 9{x}_{1}-9{x}_{2}-9{x}_{3}=0 \\ {x}_{1}+2{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 9 & -9 & -9 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-9){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & -9 & -27 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:=(-\frac{1}{9}){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $2$nd one). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=-2{x}_{3}.$ From the second equation, we get ${x}_{2}=-3{x}_{3}.$ Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{3} \\ -3{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{3}=1,$ we get the following eigenvector:

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, $\frac{b}{c}=\frac{-3}{1}=-3.$

q-37399.name: Question 2
q-37399.problem:
$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,A=[\begin{aligned}21 & -13 & -9 \\ 20 & -12 & -9 \\ 18 & -12 & -7\end{aligned}]
$$

The vector $v$ and the matrix $A$ are given above. 
If $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =1,$ then what is the value of $\frac{a}{c}?$
q-37399.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =1.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}21 & -13 & -9 \\ 20 & -12 & -9 \\ 18 & -12 & -7\end{aligned}]-1[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}20 & -13 & -9 \\ 20 & -13 & -9 \\ 18 & -12 & -8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}20{x}_{1}-13{x}_{2}-9{x}_{3}=0 \\ 20{x}_{1}-13{x}_{2}-9{x}_{3}=0 \\ 18{x}_{1}-12{x}_{2}-8{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}20 & -13 & -9 & 0 \\ 20 & -13 & -9 & 0 \\ 18 & -12 & -8 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-\frac{9}{10}){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}20 & -13 & -9 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{3}{10} & \frac{1}{10} & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}↔{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}20 & -13 & -9 & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{3}{10} & \frac{1}{10} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{2}=\frac{1}{3}{x}_{3}.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =\frac{1}{20}(13{x}_{2}+9{x}_{3}) \\  & =\frac{1}{20}(13(\frac{1}{3}{x}_{3})+9{x}_{3}) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}{x}_{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3}{x}_{3} \\ \frac{1}{3}{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{3}=3,$ we get the following eigenvector:

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, $\frac{a}{c}=\frac{2}{3}.$

q-140719.name: Question 3
q-140719.problem:
Find an eigenvector of $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}]$
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =-3.$
q-140719.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =-3.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}]-(-3)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}5{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=0 \\ {x}_{3}=0 \\ 7{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 7 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-7){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}5 & 1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $3$rd). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{3}=0.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =\frac{-{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}}{5} \\  & =\frac{-{x}_{2}+2(0)}{5} \\  & =-\frac{{x}_{2}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{{x}_{2}}{5} \\ {x}_{2} \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=5,$ we get the eigenvector
$v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$

q-89420.name: Question 4
q-89420.problem: Find an eigenvector of $A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 3 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]$ that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =4.$
q-89420.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =4.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 3 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]-4[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=0 \\ -{x}_{2}-4{x}_{3}=0 \\ -2{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -5 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-\frac{2}{5}){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -5 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $2$nd and the $3$rd). Thus, ${x}_{1}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{3}=0.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get ${x}_{2}=0.$ Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{1}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{1}=1,$ we get the eigenvector
$v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$

q-36951.name: Question 5
q-36951.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ are eigenvectors that correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=3$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=2$ of the matrix $A,$ given above. Find the third eigenvector ${v}_{3}=[a,\,b,\,c]^{T}$ such that the set $\{{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}\}$ is linearly independent. What is the value of $\frac{b}{c}?$
q-36951.worked_solution:
Since $A$ is a diagonal matrix, we have that its eigenvalues are the entries in the main diagonal, that is, ${\lambda }_{1}=3,$ ${\lambda }_{2}=2$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=-1.$ 

Also, since we obtained three distinct eigenvalues, the set of eigenvectors $\{{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}\},$ where each vector corresponds to different eigenvalue, will be linearly independent.

Now, recall that ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=3$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=2.$ Thus, the third eigenvector ${v}_{3}$ must correspond to ${\lambda }_{3}=-1.$ 

To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =-1.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]-(-1)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}=0 \\ 3{x}_{2}=0 \\ 0=0\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the augmented matrix $M$ is already in row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $2$nd one). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the first and second equations, we obtain ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}=0.$  Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{3}=1,$ we get the following eigenvector:

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, $\frac{b}{c}=\frac{0}{1}=0.$

q-140720.name: Question 6
q-140720.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ are eigenvectors that correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=2$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-3$ of the matrix $A,$ given above. Find the third eigenvector ${v}_{3}=[a,\,b,\,c]^{T}$ such that the set $\{{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}\}$ is linearly independent. What is the value of $\frac{a}{b}?$
q-140720.worked_solution:
Since $A$ is an upper triangular matrix, we have that its eigenvalues are the entries in the main diagonal, that is, ${\lambda }_{1}=2,$ ${\lambda }_{2}=-3$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=1.$ 

Also, since we obtained three distinct eigenvalues, the set of eigenvectors $\{{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}\},$ where each vector corresponds to different eigenvalue, will be linearly independent.

Now, recall that ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=2$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-3.$ Thus, the third eigenvector ${v}_{3}$ must correspond to ${\lambda }_{3}=1.$ 

To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =1.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]-1[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & -4 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=0 \\ -4{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=0 \\ 0=0\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the augmented matrix $M$ is already in its row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & -4 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{2}=\frac{1}{4}{x}_{3}.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =-{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3} \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}{x}_{3}+2{x}_{3} \\  & =\frac{7}{4}{x}_{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{7}{4}{x}_{3} \\ \frac{1}{4}{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{3}=4,$ we get the following eigenvector:

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 1 \\ 4\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, $\frac{a}{b}=\frac{7}{1}=7.$
